summary.text: Gary Palmer is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2014. Before Congress he spent roughly 25 years leading the Alabama Policy Institute, a conservative think tank he co-founded. In the House he chaired the Republican Policy Committee from 2019 to 2025 and now chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee of the Energy and Commerce Committee; he is seeking re-election after winning the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Born in 1954 in Alabama; earned a bachelor's degree in operations management from the University of Alabama in 1977.

In 1989 co-founded the Alabama Family Alliance, which became the Alabama Policy Institute, a conservative think tank; he served as its president for 25 years, stepping down in 2014 to run for Congress.

Helped found the State Policy Network, an umbrella organization of state-level think tanks, and served as its president; also served on Governor Robert Bentley's Alabama Commission on Improving State Government.

Entered the 2014 race for the 6th District after 11-term Republican Rep. Spencer Bachus announced his retirement; finished second in a seven-candidate Republican primary, won the runoff 64%-36%, and won the general election with 76% against Democrat Mark Lester.

Took office January 3, 2015, and has been re-elected since. Committee assignments for 2025-2026 are Energy and Commerce (chair of the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee) and Oversight and Government Reform.
Chaired the House Republican Policy Committee from 2019 to 2025; is listed as a member of the House Freedom Caucus.
Won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary with 85.7% of the vote over Case Dixon, after the original May primary results were voided.
